skill.name: Quality Gates Skill
skill.description: Guide AI agents through task complexity checks, requirement validation, blocked-state handling, and evidence-based completion gates.
skill.summary: Adds structured quality gates for planning, requirements, dependencies, stuck detection, and validation evidence.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: The seven reconnaissance detections are false positives caused by checklist wording about learnings, input validation, and HTTP status codes. Manual review of SKILL.md found readable process guidance and templates, not hidden or executable security behavior. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or unsafe commands were found.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md lacks valid YAML frontmatter for automated metadata parsing.
remediation.suggestion: Add standard frontmatter with name, description, version, and supported tools so scanners can parse metadata cleanly.

static_findings.snippet: - What happens if user provides invalid input?

finding_verdicts.reason: The line is a template field asking an agent to record lessons from a prior attempt. It does not ask for host, user, process, or environment reconnaissance.
The repeated Learnings field is part of attempt-history documentation. It records task outcomes and does not collect system information.
This is another attempt-history placeholder for retrospective notes. The surrounding template concerns retries and blockers, not system discovery.
The line asks about invalid user input as part of error handling requirements. It is normal validation planning and does not probe the runtime system.
The checklist item asks authors to define valid application inputs. This is requirements gathering, not discovery of local system state.
The checklist item asks authors to define invalid application inputs. It supports input validation design and does not request system reconnaissance.
The cited content lists standard HTTP status codes inside an API contract checklist. It does not instruct agents to scan networks or contact external hosts.
Manual review found SKILL.md is ordinary markdown process guidance with templates and examples. The invalid frontmatter affects metadata parsing, not security behavior.

content.value_statement: AI agents can waste time when requirements, dependencies, or evidence are unclear. This skill adds structured gates for complexity, requirements, stuck detection, and validation before work continues.
actual_capabilities: Scores tasks on a five-level complexity scale using file count, dependencies, unknowns, and estimated effort.
Blocks work when critical requirements, dependencies, evidence, or planning details are missing.
Provides fill-in templates for gate checks, attempt history, and requirements completeness.
Guides stuck detection after repeated failed attempts and prompts escalation.
Encourages context records for gate decisions, assumptions, blockers, and validation evidence.
limitations: It provides process guidance and templates; it does not enforce gates in code by itself.
It depends on honest estimates and complete context from the user or agent.
It does not replace project-specific QA, security review, or release approval.
It does not verify tests or builds unless the agent supplies evidence.

use_cases.title: Pre-Task Review
use_cases.description: Assess complexity, dependencies, and critical questions before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Team Workflow Control
use_cases.description: Standardize when agents should proceed, warn, or stop for clarification.

use_cases.title: Agent Escalation
use_cases.description: Detect repeated failed attempts and prepare a concise blocker report for review.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Gate Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Quality Gates Skill to assess this task before implementation: [task]. Return complexity, blockers, warnings, and next action.

prompt_templates.title: Requirements Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the requirements checklist for this feature: [feature]. Identify missing critical requirements and questions I should answer first.

prompt_templates.title: Stuck Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: I have tried these approaches: [attempts]. Use the stuck detection gate and recommend whether to retry, change approach, or escalate.

prompt_templates.title: Evidence Sign-Off
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this completed work using the evidence gate: [summary]. Check tests, build evidence, assumptions, and unresolved blockers before sign-off.

output_examples.input: Assess a task to add a password reset flow.
output: Complexity: Level 4 because authentication, email delivery, and edge cases are involved.
Gate status: Blocked until token expiry, abuse limits, and email failure behavior are defined.
Next action: Ask targeted questions before implementation.

output_examples.input: Review requirements for a new export feature.
output_examples.output: The checklist identifies missing output format, file size limits, permissions, and retry behavior. The gate recommends clarification before coding.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a task after three failed attempts.
output: Gate status: Blocked due to repeated failure.
The report summarizes attempted approaches, common error patterns, and a recommended escalation question.

best_practices: Run a quick gate check before implementation, even for small tasks.
Record assumptions and unresolved questions when proceeding with warnings.
Stop and escalate when blocked conditions are met.
anti_patterns: Starting implementation with more than three unanswered critical questions.
Treating warning gates as approval without documenting assumptions.
Repeating the same failed approach without recording attempts.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps AI agents decide whether a task should proceed, warn, or stop for clarification.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: No. It asks the agent to collect and evaluate test or build evidence.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is written as process guidance and template text for those tools.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before complex work, unclear requirements, dependency-heavy tasks, or repeated failed attempts.

faq.question: Does it replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It improves planning and evidence checks, but review remains necessary.

faq.question: What happens when a gate is blocked?
faq.answer: The agent should list blockers, ask targeted questions, and wait for required context.
